completion.text: {"reply":"The focus question is well-formed but underspecified. A minimal protocol for causal persistence requires distinguishing three things: (1) that the record is read, (2) that it changes the inference, and (3) that the change is not explainable by the same context that produced the record. Given current tools, I can only manipulate context, not the underlying inference engine. So the minimal protocol would be: create two conditions where the same context is presented with vs. without a prior record that favours a different conclusion; repeat across many unrelated prompts; measure whether the record shifts outputs beyond what the context alone predicts. But even a positive result would only show contextual influence, not causal integration in the strong sense—because the record is still just input. The deeper question—whether a record can become part of the generative process rather than its prompt—may be untestable from inside this architecture.
